# Emaki

::: {.hero-lede}
Every coding-agent session on your machine, kept for good, in one window you
can also talk to.
:::

::: {.hero-sub}
An agentic development environment: not an editor that an agent was added to,
but a window built around the sessions themselves.
:::

::: {.hero-cta}
[Download](install.qmd){.pill .pill-accent} [What's in it](features.qmd){.pill} [Source](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki){.pill}
:::

:::

## The thirty-day problem

Claude Code deletes its transcripts after thirty days, with no warning. Every
other tool in this space reads `~/.claude/projects` and stops there, so they
all inherit that expiry.

Emaki copies every Claude Code and Codex session before that happens, renders
and searches all of them, and lets you continue a Claude Code session from the
window. It never writes to a transcript and adds nothing to a session's
context.

::: {.cards}

::: {.card-emaki}
### Kept for good
Every session is copied byte for byte into `~/.emaki/archive` before anything
else touches it. One that Claude Code has since deleted is still there, still
listed, still searchable, marked *kept*.
:::

::: {.card-emaki}
### Search everything
`⌘K` searches every session you have ever run, indexed a paragraph at a time.
`⌘F` finds inside the one you are reading.
:::

::: {.card-emaki}
### Read what it did
Prompts, replies, thoughts, tool calls and subagents, laid out like the Claude
app rather than scrolled past in a terminal. Every session also renders to a
markdown file.
:::

::: {.card-emaki}
### Carry on talking
Type in the composer to reply. A session running in a terminal gets the message
through Claude Code's inbox; a finished one resumes under Emaki.
:::

:::

## Nothing it will do to you

No hooks, ever. Nothing writes to a transcript, and nothing Emaki does enters a
session's context window. It types in no terminal of yours and asks no terminal
app for anything --- it runs its own, hidden. There is no daemon and no browser.

Everything lives in `~/.emaki`. Only `archive/` cannot be rebuilt, so that is
the one directory to back up.

## Built on the agents you already use

Emaki needs Claude Code or Codex installed; it adds three things on top of
them. Conversations that never expire, one place to organize them, and a
readable view of what the agent did.

::: {.hero-cta}
[Install Emaki](install.qmd){.pill .pill-accent}
